R9635.summary: Alonso Sánchez, imperial ambassador at Venice, to Charles V: the money owed by Venice under the treaty ('mas de xv mil ducados', 'allende de los otros xviii mil'), restitution of goods, 'los de esta republica' (calendared by Bergenroth, CSP Spain 2 no. 476). Edited against Tomokiyo's published key; only ll. 1-3, 6, 7, 14, 22 of f. 20r and the opening of f. 21 are given, cipher groups and reading side by side.
R9635.en:
Seeing that letters from Your Majesty were so long [?already] in coming, and since nothing can be lost by it, I went
to the lords of this Republic and told them that they knew well that by the capitulation of the truce which they have
concluded with Your Majesty they were to pay, on the first of this month, another 20,000 ducats, besides the other
18,000 that they owe from last year; and that I asked them to be pleased to pay them and fulfil what they are bound to.
They answered me what they had answered before: that their lands should be restored to them, as is agreed in the said
capitulation. I replied to them that the lands were in the power of the lord Infante, and they answered that, whoever
might hold them, Your Majesty had promised to restore them.

R9653.summary: Sánchez to Charles V: the clear middle gives the news of the siege of Rhodes from the Signoria's letters (fifty thousand Turks dead, the defenders hoping for relief); the two cipher lines at the foot are read with the published key; the six-line head paragraph is illegible at DECODE's resolution.

R9613.summary: Sánchez to Charles V: his audience with the Signoria on the imperial reply to their peace paper (paper against paper; the Venetians complain the Emperor leaves the peace-and-league negotiation for a new truce, and that the Infante Ferdinand may enter the truce but not the peace); the Pregadi's debate on Cremona; French boasts and Lescun's news of 600 lances and 12,000 Gascons at Turin; the Turk not arming at sea, Rhodes holding out, Venice selling offices; the Viceroy of Naples at Mantua.
R9613.en:
I received Your Majesty's letter of the last of last month and went to the lords of this Republic. I told them that
their ambassador had discussed the peace in this way and handed in a paper, to which a reply was given on Your
Majesty's behalf in another paper, of all of which they would certainly have had a copy from their ambassador; that I
informed them that Your Majesty was well disposed, provided they came to honest and reasonable conditions, because, as
Your Majesty is emperor and head of the Christian commonwealth, so you desired more than anyone to establish and set
peace in it, especially in Italy, and to unite its forces against the infidels and Turks; that I was well instructed in
the whole negotiation and in Your Majesty's will in it; if they wished to discuss it with me, all of them or by
deputing some persons for it, they should do so, or see what seemed good to them;

R9641.summary: Sánchez to Charles V: the Signoria content with the Pope's answer on quartering imperial troops in the Gera d'Adda; the papal nuncio at Venice says the Pope could bring Venice round, but the hope of an Anglo-imperial settlement with France keeps them irresolute; postscript: Girolamo Adorno's letter and the Emperor's of 26 Sept announcing Adorno's coming with powers.
R9641.en:
I have written to the Duke of Sessa that the lords of this Republic say they are content with what the Pope answered
their ambassador on the complaint they made about the quartering of Your Majesty's army in the Ghiara d'Adda; I marvel
that, in a matter touching Your Majesty, the Pope should answer these men favourably, and this manner of answer that
the Pope gives them is harmful to this negotiation. If it could be obtained from His Holiness, it would be well that
this were provided for once and for all: that when their ambassadors speak to him about matters touching Your Majesty,
he should answer so that they know His Holiness has no less care for Your Majesty's affairs than for his own, and that
if they draw close to Your Majesty His Holiness will look after them, and if they do the contrary he will look on it
with disfavour, not as suits them. And Your Majesty should know:

R9593.summary: Sánchez to Charles V: letters of Don Juan Manuel and Geronimo Adorno sent on; his audience with the Signoria on the passage of the lansquenets through Val Camonica (he had not believed the reports until those conducting them wrote and signed them; Andrea Gritti's officer and the damage claimed); the French have taken Caravaggio, the Swiss at Monza said to be 16,000 and 4,000.

R9607.summary: Sánchez to Charles V: Venice's armament after the French defeat in Lombardy (galleys at Venice and in Candia, French soldiers come from Milan to Padua); Cremona, Lautrec and Prospero Colonna; his demand that the Signoria declare itself released from its capitulation with France; news of the Turk's fleet from Corfu (letters of 5 April) and of the King of France coming in person; the Hungarian ambassador's departure; the Signoria's minute of its answer. Uncalendared; opening line printed by Tomokiyo (2025).
R9607.en:
Brice Dudout (Claude Opus 5.5), 12 Nov 2026, from R9607reading.md (read in part, 79.5 % of 1,555 words). […] marks
words not read; italics mark probable readings. Paragraphs follow the null signs of the cipher.

f. 65r. To Your Majesty's letter of 29 April, which I received on […], there is nothing to answer, except that in the
[…] principal it is now some days since I have spoken, still less now that those of this Republic would speak, […]
since they have seen the […] they were waiting for and were in need, and […] very […] for fear and suspicion. […]
their ambassador's petition to Your Majesty […] which Your Majesty has not wished […] bad for them; and the cause,
I understand, […] the Infante […] here, and they sent to send it to their lands […] They told me they were keeping
[…] not to have them when they need them.

R9610.summary: Sánchez to Charles V: 24,000 ducats sent by the Viceroy of Naples for Prospero Colonna to pass through Venetian lands (the Signoria refuses a safe-conduct but has the rectors of Verona escort it); a safe-conduct for the Viceroy and his company; letters of the King of France from Lyon (he will not leave the enterprise, blames Lautrec, sends the Admiral); Lautrec, Cremona and Andrea Gritti; Lautrec leaves for France; the Turk's ambassador as a spy, the Turk arming a hundred sails, Venice's fifty galleys; a procurator of San Marco made for money; the Turks before Knin. Uncalendared; opening line printed by Tomokiyo (2025).
R9610.en:
A summary, not a translation, of R9610textes.md (read in part, 79.3 %; unresolved words left out). Brackets mark
what the unresolved words leave uncertain.

f. 132r. Yesterday afternoon Sánchez had letters from Banisio at Trento by a post: the Viceroy of Naples had sent
there a man with 24,000 ducats that Prospero [Colonna] had asked for, to be taken to the camp; once in Mantua [the
Marquis] would forward it, but to pass it through the Signoria's lands Banisio asked Sánchez to obtain a safe-conduct.
The Signoria answered that they could not give a safe-conduct, but would write to the rectors of Verona to send [an
escort] so that the money could pass safely through their lands, and asked that those carrying it warn the rectors of
Verona when they would be in the Signoria's lands, so that men would be there to accompany them. He writes so to
Banisio by this post.

R9614.summary: A copy (treslado, sent by Genoa to Geronimo Adorno) of the letter of 18 June sent by post to England, CSP Spain 2 no. 429, which this target already holds as R9613 from its contemporary decipherment; read here again from the cipher with the key unchanged.
R9614.en:
A summary, not a translation, of R9614textes.txt (read in part: 77.3 % strict, 87.7 % with the † words; unresolved
words left out). Brackets mark what the unresolved words leave uncertain. Key unchanged (PREREGlot3 measure FAIL).
Clear in the letter: the date "de venecia a xviij de junio de dxxij" and a postscript: this is a copy of another letter
sent "con las postas" to England, now sent by way of Genoa, addressed to Geronimo Adorno. P4 left is a separate letter in
clear, in another hand (Viceroy of Naples, Mantua, Verona, Prospero), not read here.

f. 208r. Sánchez has His Majesty's letters of the end of last month. He went to the Signoria and told them that their
ambassador [at court] had [treated] of peace and handed in a writing, answered on His Majesty's side by another writing;

R9640.summary: Sánchez to Charles V: the detention of Venetian goods in England, the French ambassador's complaints and threats, the Signoria's answers, Geronimo Adorno's plan (an enterprise against France with English money) carried by Geronimo Centurion, Don Juan Manuel, the Turk and Rhodes. Uncalendared.
R9640.en:
A summary of R9640textes.txt, not a translation. The letter is read in part: 71.5 % strict, 80.1 % with the † words.
Unresolved words are left out, and brackets mark what they leave uncertain. Daniel's key is unchanged: the PREREGlot3
measure failed, so no code value was added.

f. 139r. The [galleys] of the Venetians are detained in England, and this has made them very [uneasy]. Even those
who [govern] say openly that, because of it, they are in no state to act for France. The French party in Venice says
it cannot reach an understanding with His Majesty, because it has no one to trust. [The Pope?] (hod) was to have
been the mediator and the guarantor of the agreement between the two sides, but how could they trust him when those of
the French party draw everything to their own ends? The members of the [Council] are very [cautious] and dare not speak
out.

R9647.summary: Sánchez to Charles V: the French party at Venice holding back letters, the Signoria's answer to Sánchez and the English ambassador (no obligation left to France, complaints of the detention of its goods), its letter to its nuncio for a universal peace. Clear date a vij de noviembre. Uncalendared.
R9647.en:
A summary, not a translation, of R9647textes.txt (read in part, 75.6 % strict; unresolved words left out). Brackets
mark what the unresolved words leave uncertain. The clear date at the foot of f. 258v reads a vij de noviembre
(DECODE: 6 Nov).

f. 257r. The Signoria receives letters from France often; a few days ago some came by way of [...], and those of
the French party hold back their letters so that what they are doing is not known. Their news: French affairs are
going [well]; the army of His Majesty and of [the Pope?] withdrew without doing anything; the French will come this
[winter] to the enterprise of [Milan?]; the King of France [is coming?] and must pay his men the money promised them
by Candlemas, so that the enterprise is to be made at once. Sánchez knows nothing certain, but the Republic may be
[helping] the French with money.
